target_customer: Individual consumers seeking journaling and mental wellness tools, paying for a premium subscription
problem: People struggle to understand what influences how they feel and to build a daily reflection habit. Stoic offers short morning and evening journaling and exercises.
business_model: Consumer mobile app, freemium with annual premium subscription ($27.99 per year at 2019 launch coverage)

founders.name: Maciej Lobodzinski
previous_startups: Prismake (software agency, later acquired by Tango Agency)
founders.background_notes: YC page: builds the app; Prismake built iOS apps for clients such as dscout, Talixo and Roam Robotics.

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer iOS and Android journaling app built by a single experienced app developer; standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Journaling apps are easy to copy; advantage lies in brand, content and app store ranking. Moat type brand is my own label for that.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Stoic; the app is still active with a long tail of alternatives.

market_need_then: Mental health and wellness apps were growing in 2019 and Stoic reached App of the Day features; usage claims of over 4 million downloads are company stated.

branding.name_origin: TechCrunch (2019-08-20) says the name reflects the founder's interest in classical Stoic philosophy; the app includes quotes from Stoic philosophers.
branding.domain_note: Uses getstoic.com, not the exact stoic.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Calm and reflective: Your Journal for a Healthier Mind.

branding.brand_signature: Daily reflections app named for Stoicism
branding.community_and_virality: Featured as App of the Day in 100+ countries and reviewed by TechCrunch, per the company site; claims 4.8 App Store rating.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive real word that matches the product and a strong App Store presence, though many other stoicism apps share the name theme.

outcome_analysis: Stoic is a lean solo founder consumer app that has stayed active since its 2019 YC demo day, with company reported downloads above 4 million and a high App Store rating. No funding rounds or exit are public, so it looks like a capital efficient subscription business rather than a venture scale story.
notes: Aggregators list conflicting funding totals ($150K Craft; $271K VCBacked which may be a different company); treated as unverified, not rounds. A third party analytics page estimated about 40,000 downloads, contradicting the 4M company claim. No dated competitor source found near the 2019 batch: TechCrunch named none; later roundups discuss Daylio, Reflectly and Day One but are 2026 affiliate content, so the competitor list is left empty. The getstoic about page fetch was rate limited, so no team details beyond YC and TechCrunch.
